referenceSources.title: Ferrari F50 GT: The GT1 Race Car With an F1 Engine That Never Got To Compete - autoevolution
referenceSources.description:
A striking red Ferrari F50 GT is displayed head-on against a dark background, resting on a classic black-and-white checkered floor. The car’s sculpted hood vents, large oval headlights, and central air intake emphasize its racing pedigree, while the fixed roof scoop and massive rear wing hint at its aerodynamic enhancements.

Born from Ferrari’s ambition to dethrone the McLaren F1 GTR in the mid-1990s BPR Global GT Series, the F50 GT combined a 4.7-liter Tipo F130B engine—derived from a 1990 Formula 1 power unit—with extensive chassis and bodywork modifications. Although only three of the planned six cars were completed and tested, FIA rule changes rendered the project obsolete before it could compete, leaving the F50 GT as one of Maranello’s rarest and most formidable prototypes.
